nutshell: Today's items show AI moving into everyday products and workflows, from browser assistants with open-weight models to agents that approve code and operate databases. Security and governance concerns are rising alongside it, including agent mistakes in production databases, rules files that fail as boundaries, and fears that AI could erode online security. Research keeps pushing on agent benchmarks, video and world models, and reliable evaluation, while chip supply and export controls shape the hardware side.

items.title: Show HN: I wrote an entire Vim manual over 4 years

When I started using Vim more than a decade ago, I wished there was a manual out there teaching how to use this fantastic editor step by step, beginning with the foundations up to more advanced features. Of course at the time I did the vimtutor, but it was too dense for me to remember much from it. I also read the entire Vim manual (`:help manual`), but I didn't like it: it was too detailed in places (for example `02.8 Finding help` completely lost me for a while), and other features didn't get the treatment they deserved. items.title: Show HN: bouncemarket – a live prediction market game for a bouncing ball
items.snippet: a ball will fall. trade on where it lands. I made this game! Some technical details: The entire drop of the ball is simulated server-side, then streamed to each client as server-sent events with a small buffer. Every drop is deterministic from its starting position, so rounds can be replayed exactly for later analysis, but tiny variations in starting position can change the ultimate outcome. There's some AI traders to keep the market moving, but they drop out in any round that has more than five people. They operate using a naive set of rules that I wrote for them, so they're not too hard to beat -- it's when the market is full of real people that it gets tricky. Curious to get feedback on anything you would change, and especially whether the mechanics were clear right away or not.
items.summary: Bouncemarket is a Show HN prediction-market game for a bouncing ball, with server-side deterministic simulation streamed via server-sent events.
